# Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

Meta.content:
Updatesrc/modules/llms/server/openai/models/metaai.models.ts with latest model definitions.

Referencesrc/modules/llms/server/llm.server.types.ts and src/modules/llms/server/models.mappings.ts for context only. Focus on the model file, do not descend into other code. The vendor's protocol facts live in kb/modules/LLM-metaai-responses.md; the adapter deviations are the metaai row of _RSP_DIALECT_QUIRKS in src/modules/aix/server/dispatch/chatGenerate/adapters/openai.responsesCreate.ts.

Primary Sources: dev.meta.ai/docs. Appending.md to any docs URL returns raw markdown that plain curl fetches (no auth, no browser needed).

- Doc index: https://dev.meta.ai/llms.txt (numerous pages incl. cookbook and API reference; onecurl loop mirrors the whole set when a deep read is needed)
- Models, tiers, modalities, context windows: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models.md
- Pricing and rate limits: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits.md - Standard vs Contributor per-token tables, the search-grounding surcharge, per-image and per-hour prices, RPM/TPM per tier
- Reasoning effort ladder: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning.md
- Responses API: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses.md; full schema https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/responses/schemas.md (5,300 lines - grep it, don't read it)
- Capability pages to diff againstinterfaces / parameterSpecs: tool-calling.md, tool-search.md, search-grounding.md, structured-output.md, image-understanding.md, video-understanding.md, file-handling.md, image-generation.md, prompt-caching.md
- Release dates (the API carries none): the research.meta.ai/blog index (every Muse post, dated), ai.meta.com/blog, and Wikipedia's "Muse Spark" page (prose dates only; its release table is gone). Known: Spark 1.1 2026-07-09, Muse Image 2026-07-07, Spark 1.2 2026-08-05, Glimmer 2026-08-10, Spark 1.3 2026-09-02, Wonder 1.0 2026-10-12, Spark Open 2026-10-15.
- There is NO Model API changelog (muse-code/changelog.md is the CLI's). Third-party trackers (llm-stats.com/models/muse-spark-1.3, openrouter.ai/meta/muse-spark-1.3) are fallbacks for dates and benchmarks only.

Do NOT use web search for facts. Fetch the URLs directly; search only to locate release announcements.

Known gaps and traps (verified 2026-10-21):

- GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{id} return only {id, object, created: 0, owned_by: 'meta'}: created is a constant 0 (useless for pubDate or ordering, despite models.md claiming otherwise) and there is no type/modality field. The list does not establish what a model IS - cross-check every id against models.md before curating it as chat.
- The list mixes families:muse-image-1.0 (image output over Responses; curated with LLM_IF_Outputs_Image + LLM_IF_HOTFIX_NoStream) and muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 (ASR on /v1/asr, 404 on /v1/responses; dropped via _METAAI_NON_CHAT_PREFIXES). A new non-chat family goes in that deny-list or gets curated with the right output interfaces.
- -contributor ids are the same model at ~12x/21x lower rates and Meta trains on prompts and completions: keep them hidden: true with the tradeoff in description; never a default pick.
- maxCompletionTokens is undocumented: 131072 is Meta's advertised figure (quickstart / coding-agents configs); the server accepts max_output_tokens up to 1M, so do not derive it from probes.
- Docs print keys asLLM|... while served keys are LLM_...: validateSetup accepts both, do not tighten.

Live endpoint (extra signal): If.env.api-keys has METAAI_API_KEY, scan the served list for new ids: curl https://api.meta.ai/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $METAAI_API_KEY". Never commit or echo the key.

Probing tips:

- Effort domain:POST /v1/responses with {"model":"<id>","input":"pong","max_output_tokens":64,"reasoning":{"effort":"<v>"}}. A bad value 400s with unknown variant X, expected one of ... (the full server enum); a value the model rejects 400s with does not support "<v>" with this model. As of 2026-10-21 the enum is none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max; none is rejected on every Spark and Wonder, max is accepted on Wonder, Spark 1.3 and 1.3-contributor (the docs exclude the latter, but it honors it - offered). The rejection message lists the model's supported values. Omitted effort runs as high.
- Unknown TOP-LEVEL request params 400 withunknown parameter X - cheap discovery of new fields; unknown nested keys are silently ignored.
- tool_choice accepts only auto; truncation only disabled; logprobs are unreachable while reasoning is on.
- Temperature 2.0 is accepted but degenerate (ramblingincomplete replies, occasional HTTP 500) - the sweep records 0..1.5; do not read a 500 there as an outage.
- End-to-end ablations through the real pipeline (tools, search, reasoning, image output):npx tsx tools/develop/aix-protocol-lab/lab.ts capture metaai-responses <hello|reason|fc|search|interleave> [--model <id>] [--no-stream]
- Parameter acceptance sweep:tools/develop/llm-parameter-sweep/sweep.sh --dialect metaai --key $METAAI_API_KEY --model-filter muse-spark writes llm-metaai-parameters-sweep.json; then /llms:verify-parameters metaai diffs it against the definitions.

Important:

- Review the full model list for additions, removals, and price changes
- Minimize whitespace/comment changes, focus on content
- Preserve comments to make diffs easy to review
- Flag broken links or unexpected content

Meta.content:
# Meta AI (metaai) over the Responses dialect

Vendormetaai ("Meta AI"; the product is the Meta Model API at dev.meta.ai) serves the Muse models at https://api.meta.ai/v1 behind a bearer key. big-AGI drives every Meta model over the OpenAI Responses dialect (chatGenerate.dispatch.ts, RESPONSES_ONLY_DIALECTS), reusing aixToOpenAIResponses (Meta row in _RSP_DIALECT_QUIRKS) and createOpenAIResponsesEventParser('metaai'); metaai is one of the AixWire_Vendors.RSP_VENDORS (aix.wiretypes.ts), the Responses vendors that share the wire format but keep a private _vnd namespace for continuity state. Everything below was measured on the wire on 2026-09-02; docs are https://dev.meta.ai/docs/<page>.md (index docs/llms.txt) and disagree with the wire where marked.

## Catalog

- GET /v1/models lists 9 ids (2026-10-21) with created: 0 on all and no type/modality field. Chat: muse-wonder-1.0, muse-spark-1.3|1.2|1.1 plus -contributor twins of 1.3 and 1.2. Image output: muse-image-1.0. ASR only: muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 (404 model_not_found on /v1/responses); segmentation: sam-3.1 - both filtered by prefix.
- Uncurated ids are guessed by line (muse-<line>-<version>[-contributor]): a new version inherits context, interfaces and params from its newest curated sibling of the same tier, never the price; Contributor ids stay hidden. An unknown line gets a null context window, which keeps it off the llm-registry-sync push.
- Wonder (preview): 1,048,576 context, same inputs and request surface as Spark; $4 in / $20 out / $0.20 cached per 1M, Standard only (no Contributor tier on the API). Muse Wonder Full is Muse Code only;max effort does not select it.
- Spark: 1,048,576 context, text/image/video/PDF/audio in (1.3 audio degraded), text out. Standard $1.25 in / $4.25 out / $0.15 cached per 1M; Contributor $0.10 / $0.20 / $0.002 and Meta trains on prompts and completions (hidden by default; 150 RPM / 3M TPM vs 3,000 / 4M per team on Standard). Web search +$2.50 per 1K queries. Muse Image $0.01 per image, aspect ratio only.
- Release dates are editorial (Spark 1.1 2026-07-09, Muse Image 2026-07-07, 1.2 2026-08-05, 1.3 2026-09-02, Wonder 1.0 2026-10-12);/llms:update-models-metaai holds the source list.
- Open weights, not on the API: Muse Spark Open (816B-A42B, 2026-10-15; effortlow|medium|high|xhigh, default xhigh, reasoning always on) and Muse Glimmer (30B dense, 2026-08-10; effort low|medium|high|xhigh, default high, reasoning always on). OpenRouter's meta/muse-spark-open and meta/muse-glimmer-30b take pubDate, interfaces and effort from llmOrtMetaLookup (_ortOpenWeightMetaModels).

## Request contract

- Unknown top-level parameters 400 (unknown parameter X); unknown nested keys are ignored. seed, stop, n, logit_bias, response_format, top-level verbosity, conversation all 400. The adapter's zod strip keeps the body clean.
- tool_choice: only auto (none, required, named 400). Tools policy any degrades to auto for this dialect, with a steering hint appended to instructions.
- Underauto, every Muse model writes one commentary line before a function call; reasoning.summary moves it into a reasoning item on Wonder 1.0, Spark 1.2 and 1.1, not on Spark 1.3. Callers that expect a single call skip leading text.
- Spark 1.1 can leak its call markup as text instead of afunction_call item.
- Through OpenRouter, the Meta-served ids rejecttool_choice: 'required' as well; the Chat Completions adapter sends auto for every OpenRouter model.
- truncation: only disabled (auto 400, schema notwithstanding).
- reasoning.effort: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh, plus max on muse-wonder-1.0, muse-spark-1.3 and 1.3-contributor (the docs exclude the latter, but it honors max: 2026-10-15, ~4x the reasoning tokens of xhigh). 1.1, 1.2 and 1.2-contributor 400 on it. none parses but 400s on every Spark and Wonder. Omitted = high - expensive on trivial prompts (95-250 reasoning tokens for "pong"). reasoning.summary auto|concise|detailed accepted; summaries are often []. No raw reasoning text ever.
- max_output_tokens >= 16 (the adapter floors it); reasoning shares the budget - a tight cap returns status: incomplete with an EMPTY output[]. No enforced ceiling below 1M.
- store defaults to TRUE upstream. The adapter sends store: false + include: ['reasoning.encrypted_content'], the documented stateless path. include + previous_response_id is a 400 - never combine.
- Accepted:instructions, temperature 0..2 (2.0 is degenerate: rambling incomplete replies and an occasional 500 internal server error; the sweep records 0..1.5 as reliable), top_p (0,1], metadata (<= 16 pairs), user, prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier, parallel_tool_calls, max_tool_calls, text.verbosity, service_tier (normalized to auto). Spark is tuned for temperature 1.0 (initialTemperature).
- Function tools: flat{type: 'function', name, parameters}, strict defaults to false (the schema page says true - wrong), names take at most one dot. web_search takes search_context_size and user_location; the adapter's external_web_access is tolerated, filters.allowed_domains 400s. include: ['web_search_call.action.sources'] populates action.sources (URLs only), which the parser reads. The documented include: ['web_search_call.results'] instead adds an item-level results[] of {type: 'text_result', title, url, snippet} (titled, snippets empty; 2026-10-21) - not requested. code_interpreter and image_generation on Spark 400; custom 400s on every model ("not supported on this endpoint"), although tool-calling.md documents it.
- Structured output:text.format json_schema / json_object, Responses-only.
- Tool pairing is enforced both ways: an unmatchedfunction_call_output and a dangling function_call both 400 (_pairInteriorFunctionCalls covers the latter).

## Stream and items

- OpenAI-shaped SSE (event: + data: lines) terminated by a bare data: [DONE], which OpenAI's Responses does not send - the executor ignores it after the terminal event. Terminals: response.completed | response.incomplete | response.failed; a top-level error event can arrive mid-stream.
- response.output_text.done is not reliably emitted; content_part.done / output_item.done close text. response.in_progress repeats once per model iteration in tool loops (DEV diff warning only).
- Parallel function calls and web searches stream interleaved (item N+1 opens before item N closes). The parser's item-visit state machine logs DEV mismatches but decodes every call and search.
- Reasoning items are{type, id, encrypted_content, summary, status} - no content. The streamed id is composite rs_<response>:rs_<inner>; response.completed.output[].id repeats it verbatim on single-iteration responses and drops to the bare rs_<inner> in multi-iteration tool loops - treat ids as opaque. Either form replays (id is optional when encrypted_content is present). Blobs are Meta-private: they live in the metaai _vnd namespace (aix.wiretypes.ts, chat.fragments.ts) and never cross vendors - Meta 400s on a foreign or expired item.
- Assistant preamble before tool calls carriesphase: 'commentary'; captured and resent.
- web_search_call.action.open_page may lack url on failed opens (schema made nullish); web search items can carry status: 'failed'.
- muse-image-1.0 streams no item events (response.created -> response.completed only): curated LLM_IF_HOTFIX_NoStream, the NS parser reads image_generation_call.result (base64 WebP, no output_format echo - mime sniffed from the base64 magic). It accepts only the image_generation tool.

## Errors, headers, CORS

- Envelope{error: {code, message, param, type}}; code is null on validation errors - branch on type + HTTP status. 401 invalid_api_key for both a wrong and a missing key; unknown model is 404 model_not_found; 429 carries Retry-After; 504 affects non-streaming only.
- x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining}-{requests,tokens} on Spark generations only; limits are per team and per tier. x-request-id on most responses.
- CORS:access-control-allow-origin: *, allow-headers: *, methods GET,POST,DELETE,OPTIONS, on preflights and on error responses - browser-direct (CSF) works. No expose-headers, so rate-limit headers are invisible client-side.

## Deliberately not wired

- Resume / delete (GET/DELETE /v1/responses/{id}): served OpenAI-identically, but the client lever is globally off and the adapter's include gate is coupled to store: false.
- Thecomputer tool ({type: 'computer'} -> computer_call items with batched actions; Responses only, accepted by Wonder and every Spark) and the Anthropic-shaped POST /v1/messages (a stateless adapter over the Responses pipeline).
- tool_search + namespace tools, context_management / compaction items, frequency_penalty / presence_penalty, prompt_cache_retention, background, POST /v1/responses/input_tokens (its count includes ~157 injected scaffolding tokens and is not comparable to usage.input_tokens).
- input_video, input_file (PDF), input_audio parts: AIX has no native parts for them yet, so those attachments degrade to text.

Maintenance:/llms:update-models-metaai (catalog, prices), tools/develop/aix-protocol-lab flavor metaai-responses (protocol), tools/develop/llm-parameter-sweep dialect metaai + /llms:verify-parameters metaai (parameter acceptance).

Meta.description: to Meta for the LLaMA announcement this story starts from; to Ollama (MIT) ... - Meta — Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter large language model, 2023-02-24 ... Port of Facebook's LLaMA model in C/C++, with Apple Silicon support...
Meta.content:
The notes — a program hacked in an evening, who wrote it, who keeps it now, and the file format it gave the world, dated

# A short history of llama.cpp

exhibit one hundred and twelve The notes
Published 2026-11-14 (UTC)
A small (human) team and a fleet of AI agents.

One evening's hack in March 2023 that put a large language model on a laptop's processor, the small C library and the company behind it, the file format it gave the world, and the servers, apps and engines that run on it today, dated from the project's own record.

ask about this page → assistant.strata2signal.com · in beta, still being tested

hardware on this page: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) · RTX 5090 Laptop GPU (24 GB) · RTX 3090 Ti (24 GB) → research.strata2signal.com/hardware/ · the roster is in beta, still being tested

## the short version

llama.cpp is free, open-source software that runs a large language model, the kind of AI inside a chatbot, on an ordinary computer: a laptop's processor, a graphics card, a phone. Georgi Gerganov wrote the first version in what his README called an evening and published it on 2023-03-10, two weeks after Meta released its LLaMA models to researchers. It is the engine under Ollama, LM Studio and the Strata engine, the project that wrote GGUF, the file format most of Ollama's library ships in, and the program beneath most of the language-model numbers on this hub. (Despite the similar name, the Strata engine, github.com/Niko1221/Strata, is an unrelated project; strata2signal has no affiliation with it.) Its company, ggml.ai, joined Hugging Face on 2026-02-20, and its first major version, v1.0.0, was published on 2026-11-13. It sits beside our other short histories, among them Mistral, Ollama and vLLM.

3,461 words, about 16 minutes to read.

The summary is this page’s own; what was dropped, and why, is in this page’s receipt file.

If you're new here: strata→signal is a small workshop (plus a friendly dog with a white patch) that builds on its own machines and writes up what it measures. Every date below was read during a pass on 2026-10-14, 2026-10-29 or 2026-11-12, the newest on 2026-11-13 (UTC) with the project's releases, each from the source credited beside it — among them the project's own commits, pull requests, releases and announcements as GitHub records them, the ggml.ai and llama.app pages, Hugging Face's documentation and blog, Meta's announcement, Hacker News, and our own released pages. Where we found no source, the claim is not here.

Five words this page leans on. A model's weights are the numbers it learned in training, stored as files. A token is the unit a model reads and writes: a word or a piece of one. Quantization is storing the weights in fewer bits than they were trained in, so a model fits in less memory; The compressed photograph explains what that costs. GGUF is llama.cpp's single-file format for a model, usually a quantized one. A backend is the code that does the arithmetic on one kind of hardware: a processor, an NVIDIA card, an Apple chip.

## The engine under most of our numbers

On 2026-11-12 we read the markdown copy published beside each of the 108 pages on this shelf that carry one: 34 of them name llama.cpp. The doorman at the print lab and at RuleSage's rules desk runs through Ollama, and Ollama runs llama.cpp's own server underneath; A short history of Mistral credited every reading as "taken through Ollama (MIT) over llama.cpp (MIT)". Our two pages on the Strata engine benched llama.cpp itself on three cards. This page is the history behind those numbers.

## One evening in March 2023

On 2023-02-24 Meta announced LLaMA, "a state-of-the-art foundational large language model", in four sizes from 7 to 65 billion parameters, "under a noncommercial license focused on research use cases", with access "granted on a case-by-case basis" to researchers.

Two weeks later, on 2023-03-10, Georgi Gerganov made a commit titled "Initial release" (18:40:58Z) and put it on GitHub as llama.cpp. The README he wrote that evening is still in the repository's history: "Inference of Facebook's LLaMA model in pure C/C++"; "The main goal is to run the model using 4-bit quantization on a MacBook"; and, under its list of features, "This was hacked in an evening - I have no idea if it works correctly." It told users to "obtain the original LLaMA model weights" themselves; the project shipped none. How those files got out of Meta's hands that same week, and the licences that followed, is The weights that got out; this page stays with the program.

That same evening, at 20:01Z, it was on Hacker News, where "Llama.cpp: Port of Facebook's LLaMA model in C/C++, with Apple Silicon support" drew 989 points and 284 comments. The first outside fix was merged that same evening (pull request #3, 23:04Z). From there the record is the repository's own: on 2026-11-12 GitHub counts 134,490 stars and 25,503 forks, under the MIT licence.

## ggml, the library underneath, and ggml.ai, the company

llama.cpp does not do its own arithmetic. Its README says it is built on top of the ggml library, a "tensor library for machine learning" whose repository Gerganov created on 2022-09-18, a week before whisper.cpp (2022-09-25), the same organization's port of OpenAI's Whisper speech model.

Six days in, on 2023-03-16, Gerganov opened a discussion titled "Inference at the edge": "This project will remain open-source", and "Bloating the software with the ideas of today will make it useless tomorrow".

The company came the same year. ggml.ai's own page: "ggml.ai is a company founded in 2023 by Georgi Gerganov to support the development of ggml. Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross provided the pre-seed funding." The GitHub organization ggml-org, "AI inference at the edge", was created on 2023-05-22, and llama.cpp, ggml and whisper.cpp live there now; no source we read dates the move from Gerganov's own account, so this page does not.

On 2026-02-20 Gerganov announced "ggml.ai joins Hugging Face to ensure the long-term progress of Local AI": "The ggml team continues to lead, maintain and support full-time the ggml and llama.cpp libraries and related open-source projects", and "The project will continue to be 100% open-source and community driven as it is now." Hugging Face's own blog announced it the same day: "We are super happy to announce that GGML, creators of Llama.cpp, are joining HF in order to keep future AI open." The ggml.ai page says it in one line: "The company was acquired by Hugging Face in 2026."

## From GGML files to GGUF

The first format was whatever the converter wrote: a ggml-model-f16.bin, then a q4_0 copy of it. On 2023-06-05 the project merged "k-quants" (#1684), "a series of 2-6 bit quantization methods, along with quantization mixes": the Q2_K to Q6_K types.

On 2023-07-26 Gerganov opened the GGUF pull request (#2398), merged 2023-08-21: a file that describes itself, with key-value metadata beside the weights, and a breaking change, so every existing model had to be converted again. The three formats before it, the pull request's own words, the spec's later versions and what sits inside one of those files are on Inside a GGUF file, which dates each step from the memory-mapped weights of 2023-03-30 to the spec's landing in November 2023.

## The backends, dated

The first release ran on the processor. The graphics cards came in through pull requests, each dated here to its merge in GitHub's record.

Jeffrey Morgan, one of Ollama's two founders, later said "Ollama was originally inspired by the 'server' example" (our Ollama history). OpenAI-compatible routes followed on 2023-11-25 (#4198).

Today's llama-server README lists OpenAI-compatible chat, responses and embeddings routes, an Anthropic Messages route, reranking, "parallel decoding with multi-user support", multimodal input and a web UI; it listens by default on the loopback address, the one a computer uses to talk to itself, so a server that listens only there cannot be reached from another machine. 本次更新将 DeepSeek App 的各项交互功能直接整合进原有 API。开启对应参数后，相关工具调用与上下文拼接均由服务端自动完成。

目前，V4.1-Flash 模型（deepseek-flash）已在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 接口下支持以下能力：

联网搜索：在非思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可根据提问自动发起网页或图片搜索并附引用作答；

深度思考搜索：在思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可在多步推理中自主联网搜索与阅读链接；

文件输入：支持上传 PDF、Office、图片等格式的文件，完成纯文本提取或图文混排解析后，拼入对话上下文供模型作答；

阅读链接：将 deepseek_read_url 工具打开后，模型可自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答；

模型安全：开启安全校验参数后，DeepSeek 将提供基础风控，审核模型输入输出，命中风险时返回拒答标识。如您对外提供应用服务，请务必开启该参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记、AI 标识等义务。

使用上述接口，开发者即可实现与 DeepSeek App 基本一致的功能。为直观演示这一效果，DeepSeek 基于新版 API 构建并开源了一份轻量的前端 Demo，支持直接导入 DeepSeek 历史对话。

DeepSeek.title: 格局！刚刚 DeepSeek 正式开放全家桶 API，咱都能复刻 DeepSeek App 了？
DeepSeek.description: 联网搜索、深度思考搜索、阅读链接、上传文件、语音输入和朗读，开发 AI Agent 的成本又降低了 ... 简单来说，DeepSeek 把自家 App 里的联网搜索、深度思考搜索、阅读链接、上传文件、语音输入和朗读，全部开放成了 API。
DeepSeek.content:
# 格局！刚刚 DeepSeek 正式开放全家桶 API，咱都能复刻 DeepSeek App 了？

2026-11-14 2

举报

简介： DeepSeek 全家桶应用 API 一手实测，开发者真的可以 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App 了吗？联网搜索、深度思考搜索、阅读链接、上传文件、语音输入和朗读，开发 AI Agent 的成本又降低了。

大家好，我是程序员鱼皮。

昨晚 10 点多，DeepSeek 又更新了，他们怎么这么喜欢在周五下班后更新？

这次没有发布新模型，而是发布了一套「全家桶应用 API」。

简单来说，DeepSeek 把自家 App 里的联网搜索、深度思考搜索、阅读链接、上传文件、语音输入和朗读，全部开放成了 API。

你只要在原来的请求里多加一两个参数，服务端就会自己去搜索、读网页、把结果拼进上下文，不用再去对接一堆第三方工具了。

按照官方的说法，开发者可以 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App！

不过 Search 和 Fetch 两个搜索接口上个月就开放过了，这次新增的是对话里的内置联网工具、文件输入、OCR、语音和安全审核。

其实在 DeepSeek 开放这些 API 之前，网上已经有类似的 API 了，那 DeepSeek 自家的这些能力到底怎么样呢？

我把这些能力全部对接了一遍，这篇文章带大家吃一波螃蟹~

## 价格怎么算

首先，模型本身的价格没变，用的还是 V4.1 Flash，工作日高峰时段每百万 tokens 输入 2 元、输出 8 元，其他时间半价。

新增的工具则是按次单独收费：

搜索和网页抓取都是 5 元一千次，一小时的录音转文字只要 3 毛 9，而且语音识别和语音合成目前还在限时 5 折。

## 怎么接入

第一步，先到 DeepSeek 开放平台创建一个 API Key。

DeepSeek 同时兼容 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 两种协议，Chat Completions、Responses、Messages 三套接口都能用，模型名统一填deepseek-flash。

我用的是最常见的 OpenAI Python SDK，先安装依赖：
pip install openai

          AI 代码解读

然后在请求里加一个tools 参数，声明联网搜索 deepseek_web_search 和阅读链接 deepseek_read_url 两个工具。搜索和读网页都在服务端完成，客户端不用写工具调用逻辑：
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.deepseek.com")

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-flash",
    messages=[
        {
   "role": "latest_reminder", "content": "2026-11-14,星期六,上海,Web,中文"},
        {
   "role": "user", "content": "今天上海天气怎么样？适合出门吗？简短回答"},
    ],
    tools=[{
   "type": "deepseek_web_search"}, {
   "type": "deepseek_read_url"}],
    extra_body={
   "thinking": {
   "type": "disabled"}},
)

msg = resp.choices[0].message
print(msg.content)
for step in msg.model_extra["server_tool_calls"]:
    for call in step["calls"]:
        print("🔍", call["kind"], call["action"].get("queries") or call["action"].get("url"))
print("计费次数:", resp.usage.model_extra["server_tool_use"])

          AI 代码解读

运行一下，5 秒左右就拿到了答案，AI 自己搜了 3 个关键词：

代码里的那条latest_reminder 消息，作用是告诉 AI 今天几号、用户在哪儿。这条消息一定要传，不传会发生什么，后面你就知道了。

如果你懒得写代码，官方还开源了一个演示客户端，填上 API Key 就能用，还能导入 DeepSeek 网页端导出的历史对话。

## 联网搜索实测

我先问了一个昨晚才发生的事，就是 DeepSeek 全家桶 API 有哪些能力、各项工具怎么收费？

第一次我没传日期，结果 AI 把搜索词写成了「2026 年 6 月」，还一本正经地纠正我「你提到的昨晚发布可能有些误会」，说发布时间是 11 月 12 号，显然日期搞错了。

加上latest_reminder 之后，搜索词和日期都对了，5.2 秒出了结果，还附带了 13 个引用。

但还剩一处错误，AI 说官方没有公布 OCR 和语音的价格。

因为普通联网搜索只看搜索摘要，不会点开网页，而价格表恰好是公告里的一张图片。

我把同一个问题换成深度思考搜索，也就是打开thinking。这次 AI 搜了 3 个关键词，又打开了 5 个新闻网页，8.7 秒后交出了完整的价格表，没有遗漏任何细节。

换成一个窄一点的问题，只问语音合成怎么收费，两种模式就都答对了，普通搜索只用了 2.4 秒。

所以，简单的事实查询用普通搜索就够了，需要汇总好几条信息的问题再打开深度思考。

最后来个刁钻的测试，我在官方 Demo 里打开深度思考和智能搜索，问 AI：程序员鱼皮最近一个月在忙什么？

AI 一口气搜到了 26 个网页，又挑了 7 个打开阅读：

11 秒后，AI 按时间线列出了我最近发的 Gemini 4 Carbon、Claude Fable 5.2 测评和 DSH 插件推荐，日期全部对得上。

做自媒体竟然还有这个好处，啥事儿网上都能搜到，比我自己记得还清楚。

## 阅读链接实测

接下来测试 DeepSeek 阅读链接的能力，我把自己 《AI 编程教程》 的网址丢给 AI，让 AI 用 3 句话介绍一下。

6 秒后 AI 给出了回答，内容挑不出毛病。但从用量数据来看，AI 只读到了 495 个 token，也就是页面开头那一小段简介。

因为教程的章节目录是用 JS 渲染出来的，DeepSeek 抓取时不执行 JS，自然就看不到。

## 文件输入实测

测试 DeepSeek 文件输入能力的时候，我专门挖了个坑。

我把自己 《AI 编程零基础入门教程》 里的「AI 编程学习路线」这一章导出成 PDF，一共 35 页、36 MB，带了几十张图。

其中有一张思维导图标了每个阶段建议学多久，这些时长 只写在了图里：

上传解析花了 20 秒左右。我先问了一个正文里有答案的问题「作者建议新手先用哪个工具」，AI 只花 1 秒就答对了。而且再次引用这份文件时，1.6 万个 token 全部命中了缓存。

然后我问了图里的内容，阶段 1 和阶段 2 分别建议学多久，阶段 2 又列了哪几个国产 AI 编程工具。

结果翻车了。

纯文字解析和图文混排解析两种方式我都试了，AI 都说文档里找不到阶段 1 和阶段 2 的时长。。

可我把这一页单独截图交给 OCR 接口，只花了 2.3 秒，就把每个阶段的学习时长全认出来了。

也就是说，OCR 本身认得出来这些信息，是对话里的文档解析把这一页弄丢了。不过 OCR 能力也并不完美，思维导图的层级关系被认乱了，Cursor 跑到了「核心功能」的下面。

所以如果你的文档里有些关键信息藏在图片中，要用 DeepSeek API 的话，建议先单独跑一遍 OCR，再把识别出的文字交给模型。

## 语音实测

测试语音识别能力时，我用的素材是自己 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 测评视频的前 60 秒口播。

只花了 3.2 秒就识别完了，还自动加好了标点。我拿视频的字幕原稿逐字对比了一下，280 个字只错了 1 个，把「三个模式」认成了「三种模式」，准确度还是不错的。

语音合成有一男一女两个音色，首字节大约 1 秒，14 秒的音频不到 3 秒就合成好了，Markdown 加粗符号等无效内容也会被自动过滤掉。

我把合成的音频再丢回语音识别做反向检查，男声版一字不差，女声版把「Claude Code」认成了「Cloud Code」。

不过语音识别单次最长只支持 120 秒，语音合成也不能调语速，想制作长音频的话，得自己先切片。

## 对比其他 API

像我平时做 AI 应用，联网搜索和网页抓取用得最多的是 Firecrawl 插件，那 DeepSeek 的 Search 和 Fetch 接口能不能平替它呢？

我用同样的 3 个搜索词和 4 个网址，分别调用了两家的接口：

搜索速度的差距非常夸张，DeepSeek 每次 0.3 秒左右，Firecrawl 要 2.6 到 4.4 秒，快了 10 倍左右！

搜索质量两边差不多，DeepSeek 还会给每条结果打相关性分数和权威度等级，不过搜英文时会混进西班牙语和繁体版本的文档。

网页抓取方面，DeepSeek 大部分页面零点几秒就返回了，正文也更干净。Firecrawl 抓 GitHub 时混进了大量导航栏，抓我的面试鸭首页更是直接被网站防火墙拦了，只拿到报错页。。

但是 Firecrawl 会执行 JS 渲染页面，我教程网站的章节目录它能够抓到。而且 Firecrawl 还支持整站爬取、浏览器交互这些高级功能。

单论能力，还是 Firecrawl 这种专业服务更成熟。

再对比下价格。Firecrawl 最便宜的 Hobby 套餐年付每月 16 刀，换算下来，抓取一千页大约 21 元，搜索一千次大约 43 元。

而 DeepSeek 都是 5 元一千次，按量付费，还不用订阅套餐，价格上是真香。

所以我的选择是，中文网站的 AI 搜索场景直接用 DeepSeek，需要渲染 JS 或者整站爬取的时候再上 Firecrawl，应该能帮我节省不少费用。

## 最后哔哔

整体来看，我觉得 DeepSeek 全家桶的能力还是很丰富的，开发者又多了一个选择。

全家桶 API 最大的价值，是把做 AI 聊天应用的门槛又降了一大截。以前做一个能联网、读文件、语音对话的 Agent，得对接好几家服务，现在一个 API Key 就搞定了。

而且是真便宜。将近 20 次对话、两次 35 页的 PDF 解析，再加上 OCR、语音和二十多次搜索抓取，我总共只花了 5 毛多！

但是，每项能力单拎出来，跟专业服务比还是逊色一些，比如网页抓取不支持 JS 渲染，文件解析会丢掉图里的信息，语音合成不能调语速。

所以想快速做个 AI 应用，用全家桶一站式搞定很划算；如果某项能力正好是产品的核心，还是用更专业的服务。

另外，对外提供服务的话，官方要求开启safety_check 安全审核，并自己承担内容审核、大模型登记、AI 标识等义务。我试了下，开启后问 SQL 注入原理这类技术问题照样能答，没有误杀。

OK 就分享到这里，本文会收录到我免费开源的 《AI 编程零基础入门教程》，上千张图、几十万字，带你从 0 开始快速学会 AI 编程，做出自己的产品、跑通变现全流程，一次拿捏。

我是鱼皮，持续分享 AI 编程干货。觉得有用的话记得点赞收藏和关注~

# 刚刚，DeepSeek全家桶API正式开放！你也能造一个DeepSeek了

2026-11-14 03:07:09 来源: 新智元 北京 举报

0

分享至

新智元报道

就在大周五晚上，DeepSeek又搞事情了！

DeepSeek正式开放全家桶应用 API！～

以前，你在 DeepSeek App 和网页端用得最顺手的一大串功能，包括深度思考搜索、上传文件、读链接、语音交互、甚至文字识别……

现在全打包进了 API 里！

你可以在自己的应用中，轻松实现复杂对话功能。

官方甚至放话：开发者可以 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App！

周五晚上，觉是不用睡了。

什么叫「源神」？这就叫源神。

你就看看下面这个API定价，那叫一个惊喜——

评论区也瞬间炸锅了。

「什么叫 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App？？？这人工智能之光！」

「DeepSeek 真的很会为用户着想，它真的，我哭死。」

「格局太大了！」

再也不用当缝合怪了！

开发者可「躺平」了

之前，如果想从头复刻 DeepSeek，你要经历什么？

首先，你要会在本地部署大模型。

然而，光接入一个API是远远不够的，还得费老大劲，去对接外部工具、处理调用衔接。

简直像个缝合怪一样。

但今天，DeepSeek开放的全家桶API，直接帮开发者把桌子掀了！

DeepSeek App 的各项交互功能，直接整合进原有 API。所有繁琐的工具调用、上下文拼接，全由ds服务端完成。

只要开启对应参数，就能召唤出DeepSeek完全体！

在原有 API 中开启对应的参数，DeepSeek服务端自动完成相关的工具调用、上下文拼接

现在，V4.1-Flash已在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 接口下，全面支持以下能力。

联网搜索 & 深度思考搜索

非思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具，模型就能自动搜网页、搜图片，还附带引用。

开启思考模式后，更是逆天了——模型能在多步推理中自主联网搜索+阅读链接，简直逻辑拉满！

文件输入

直接丢进去 PDF、Office 文档、图片，服务端会自动纯文本提取/图文混排解析，无缝拼入对话上下文。

阅读链接

打开 deepseek_read_url 工具，用户在对话里发个链接，模型就自动抓取网页，结合上下文作答。

内置模型安全

开启安全校验参数，就直接提供基础风控，审核输入输出，还支持图片审核，让合规一步到位。

别人卖 API 好比卖水和电，DeepSeek 这是直接卖饮水厂和发电站啊！

DeepSeek 的格局远不止于此

甚至，为了方便开发者，DeepSeek 还把底层能力拆成独立接口，支持单独或组合调用！

包括：

Search（ 联网搜索）

Fetch（网页抓取）

OCR（文字识别）

ASR（语音识别）

TTS（语音合成）

从此，DeepSeek可以当成底层工具库，需要哪个调哪个，so easy~

基于这套新版 API，官方还开源了一个轻量的前端演示Demo。

它完整演示了联网搜索、深度思考、文件图片上传、朗读回答、语音输入、Markdown 与 Mermaid 图表渲染等功能……

渲染响应：Chatbot 的一次响应包含多种内容块，以上是各类块在 DeepSeek 网页端中对应的位置

甚至支持直接导入历史对话，无缝接着聊！

而且 API Key、历史对话和图片还都保存在浏览器本地，安全感拉满。

想抄作业的开发者，可以直接冲了。

在线体验入口：https://cdn.deepseek.com/chat-demo

开源代码仓库：https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo

大肥鱼这波，确实「格局打开」了

一般来说，哪个公司做了个好用的功能，恨不得藏着掖着，生怕被学了去。

但ds直接掏出压箱底的技术，不仅给工具，开源demo都直接喂到嘴边。

官方公告最后这样写：其实，我们的DeepSeek App只是个基础款。现在脏活累活交给我们，别再重复造轮子了，赶紧去整个大活吧！

自己疯狂卷技术，为大家铺路，让开发者站在自己肩膀上，去造下一个爆款。

当年，底层协议的无私共享，成就了如今的互联网。今天，DeepSeek在重塑AI时代的共享基座。

DeepSeek，不愧是人类之光啊。

DeepSeek.description: 以前大家在DeepSeek App里用得顺手的联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件上传、链接阅读等功能，现在开发者通过API通通都能直接用上了，而且不必打包使用，它们都有独立接口，支持单独调用、分别计费。
DeepSeek.content:
# 突发！DeepSeek开放全家桶API

一水 2026-11-14 10:39:56 来源：量子位

官方App功能均可自由组合调用

周五晚上搞事，D老师通通都不藏了！

就在刚刚，DeepSeek宣布，正式开放全家桶应用API。

什么意思？

以前大家在DeepSeek App里用得顺手的联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件上传、链接阅读等功能，现在开发者通过API通通都能直接用上了，而且不必打包使用，它们都有独立接口，支持单独调用、分别计费。

划重点，语音能力也首次加入开放行列，包括语音识别、语音合成等接口。

官方还放出一句相当有意思的话：

开发者甚至可以1：1复刻出完整的DeepSeek App。

不是哥们，连自家产品都允许别人照着做啊？？

DeepSeek还贴心亲自打了个样，直接开源了一套轻量级聊天前端Demo，支持导入DeepSeek历史对话。

也就是说，开发者不用再从头折腾搜索、文件解析、语音识别这些基础功能，就能快速搭出一个功能接近DeepSeek App的产品。

消息一出，评论区也是相当热闹。

有网友直接感叹：

什么叫1：1复刻出完整的DeepSeek App？？？人工智能之光！

全家桶应用API开放一览

具体来看，这次DeepSeek一口气开放了这些能力：

这里有两个变化值得单独说说。

首先，联网搜索其实不是第一次开放，早在今年10月17日，DeepSeek就已经开放了自研Search和Fetch接口。

但当时，开发者还需要自己处理不少工具调用和模型之间的衔接工作。

比如用户问“最近AI圈发生了什么”，开发者需要先让模型判断要不要搜索，再调用Search找网页、用Fetch读取内容，最后把结果重新交给模型总结。

这一整套流程，都得开发者自己写代码串起来。

现在就简单多了。

开发者只要给模型打开联网搜索功能，什么时候搜索、搜什么、要读哪些网页，以及如何根据搜索结果继续回答，DeepSeek都会自动完成。

其次是语音，这次终于有了官方独立接口。

此前，DeepSeek App虽然已经支持语音交互，但公开的模型API并没有提供同样完整的语音能力。

开发者想做一个能听会说的DeepSeek助手，通常还需要另外接入语音识别、语音合成服务。

现在，ASR和TTS都可以通过DeepSeek官方接口调用了。

而且，上述底层能力也不必全部打包使用。

DeepSeek还提供了Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS等独立接口，开发者可以按需选择、自由组合。

目前，V4.1-Flash模型已在Messages、Responses和Chat Completions三类接口下支持相关对话扩展功能。

换句话说，D老师这次是把自家App背后的整套基础能力，像积木一样全部交到了开发者手里。

那么问题来了：

功能给得这么全，价格又如何？

语音识别一小时不到4毛，DeepSeek这次还打五折

先看DeepSeek这次公布的工具API价格表：

最扎眼的，当然是语音。

语音识别原价0.78元/小时，目前直接打五折，只要0.39元。

换算下来，一分钟大约0.0065元，识别一小时录音，连4毛钱都不到。

语音合成同样五折，原价每万字符3元，现在只要1.5元。

什么概念？

对比一下国外主流厂商的语音API价格：

OpenAI的GPT-Transcribe，识别一小时音频需要0.27美元（约合人民币1.81元）。

即便是更便宜的GPT-4o mini Transcribe，也要0.18美元（约合人民币1.21元）。

Google Cloud的标准语音识别服务，按0.016美元/分钟计算，一小时是0.96美元（约合人民币6.43元）。

相比之下，DeepSeek目前的0.39元，分别只有上述三款服务价格的约1/4.6、1/3.1和1/16.5。

至于搜索和网页抓取，依旧是此前公布的每1000次成功调用5元。

文字识别OCR则为每1000页1.5元，平均识别一页只要0.0015元。

这么一看，DeepSeek这次的定价思路也挺清楚。

原有的搜索能力保持低价，新开放的语音接口再用五折优惠降低使用门槛。

对于想做语音助手、会议记录、文档处理等应用的开发者来说，至少基础工具的调用成本，已经被压到了相当低的水平。

（D老师还是你D老师）

One More Thing

最后，还有个挺有意思的细节。

DeepSeek在公告末尾写道：

DeepSeek现有的对话产品只是较为基础的一种形态。

这话倒也符合D老师一贯以来的画风。

一直以来，相比花大力气经营C端产品，DeepSeek似乎更愿意把精力放在模型研发上。

DeepSeek App虽已积累了大量C端用户，但从产品形态上看，依然是大家熟悉的聊天助手。

如今，它干脆把所有能力全部开放，甚至连复刻自家APP的示例代码都准备好，颇有一种：

模型我继续研究，应用该怎么玩，就交给大家来摸索的意思。

怎么说呢？这招还挺机智的。。。

回头看移动互联网时代，微信、抖音这些超级应用，几乎重塑了人们社交、娱乐乃至获取信息的方式。

而到了AI时代，大模型已经越来越强，应用形态却似乎还没跟上。

从ChatGPT到DeepSeek，大家最熟悉的交互方式，依然是打开一个聊天框，输入问题，等待回答。

但AI的下一款超级应用，真的还会是一个聊天框吗？

眼下谁也没有答案。

既然如此，与其自己关起门来猜，不如把工具都摆出来，让全世界的开发者一起试。

万一真有人折腾出了下一个爆款呢？

真就D老师大舞台，有脑洞你就来。（doge）

Qwen.content:
# Alibaba Cloud (Qwen)

Alibaba Cloud's DashScope API provides OpenAI-compatible access to Qwen language models. Use OpenAI provider options supported by your chosen model.

## Setup

To use Alibaba Cloud's API, set theDASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file:
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI provider options; support varies by model. Example:
providers:
  - alibaba:qwen3.8-max # Simple usage
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.7-plus # Aliases: alicloud:, aliyun:, dashscope:
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to DASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable
      apiBaseUrl: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 # Optional: Override default API base URL

note

The equivalent provider prefixes arealicloud:, aliyun:, and dashscope:. For new configurations, Alibaba recommends qwen3.7-plus for balanced use, qwen3.8-flash for lower cost, or qwen3.8-max for stronger reasoning. Check the model catalog for your region; model availability differs by region.

If you're using the Alibaba Cloud Beijing region console, switch the base URL tohttps://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 instead of the international endpoint.

## Supported Models

The built-in Alibaba provider implements OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and text embeddings. The catalog below also lists separate realtime, speech recognition, and image generation services. Listing a model here does not add those endpoints to this provider. Choose a model supported by your selected endpoint and region.

### Qwen 3 Flagship

- qwen3.8-max / qwen3.8-max-0902 - Current flagship with text, image, and video input and a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.8-flash - Faster Qwen3.8 model with a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.7-plus / qwen3.7-plus-2026-05-26 - General-purpose model with thinking, vision, and tool calling
- qwen3.7-flash / qwen3.7-flash-2026-07-15 - Lower-cost Qwen3.7 model
- qwen3.7-max / qwen3.7-max-2026-06-08 - Previous flagship
- qwen3.6-plus / qwen3.6-flash and qwen3.5-plus / qwen3.5-flash - Previous model families
- qwen3-max - Supports reasoning and tool calling
- qwen3-max-preview - Preview version with thinking mode support
- qwen3-max-2025-09-23 - September 2025 snapshot
- qwen-max - 32K context (30,720 in, 8,192 out)
- qwen-max-latest - Always updated to latest version
- qwen-max-2025-01-25 - January 2025 snapshot
- qwen-plus / qwen-plus-latest - 128K-1M context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen-plus-2025-09-11, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-plus-2025-07-14, qwen-plus-2025-04-28, qwen-plus-2025-01-25 - Dated snapshots
- qwen-flash / qwen-flash-2025-07-28 - Latency-optimized general model
- qwen-turbo / qwen-turbo-latest / qwen-turbo-2025-04-28 / qwen-turbo-2024-11-01 - Earlier low-latency model; see qwen-flash
- qwen-long-latest / qwen-long-2025-01-25 - 10M context for long-text analysis, summarization, and extraction

### Qwen 3 Omni & Realtime

- qwen3.8-omni-flash - Text output from text, image, audio, and video input through Chat Completions; use the separate realtime API for qwen3.8-omni-flash-realtime
- qwen3-omni-flash / qwen3-omni-flash-2025-09-15 - Supports speech and vision in thinking and non-thinking modes

Qwen.title: 阿里雲僅透過 Token Plan 提供 Qwen4-Max-Preview | Gate 新聞
Qwen.description: Alibaba Cloud 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日推出 Qwen4-Max-Preview，這是一款新一代多模態模型，支援文字、圖片及影片，並具備深度推理能力，可處理複雜任務。
Qwen.content:
阿里雲僅透過 Token Plan 提供 Qwen4-Max-Preview

關鍵要點

Alibaba Cloud 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日推出 Qwen4-Max-Preview，這是一款新一代多模態模型，支援文字、圖片及影片，並具備深度推理能力，可處理複雜任務。

根據 Alibaba Cloud Model Studio 文件，Qwen4-Max-Preview 的上下文長度為 100 萬個 token，且在預設啟用思考模式時，最多可輸出 393,216 個 token。

Alibaba Cloud 將 Qwen4-Max-Preview 的存取權限限制為僅供 Token Plan 用戶使用，至 2026 年 11 月 25 日；預覽期結束後，該模型預計將下架。

Alibaba Cloud 的 Qwen4-Max-Preview 自 2026 年 11 月 11 日 10:00 至 2026 年 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8）開放預覽。此模型僅能透過 Token Plan 使用，不支援隨用隨付。Alibaba Cloud 的 Model Studio 文件將 Qwen4-Max-Preview 描述為 Qwen 家族的新一代旗艦多模態模型，結合文字生成、圖像與影片理解及深度推理功能，適用於程式設計、辦公生產力、前端設計及複雜的智能代理任務。

Qwen4-Max-Preview 結合深度推理、多模態輸入與工具呼叫

此模型預設啟用思考功能，開發者可使用 reasoning_effort 參數調整推理強度。模型接受文字、圖像及影片輸入，可用於螢幕截圖分析、文件理解及影片分析。工具呼叫支援 Function Calling、網頁搜尋及內建工具；結構化輸出則支援 JSON Object 和 JSON Schema 格式。

此模型相容於 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses 及 Anthropic Messages API。其上下文長度為 100 萬個 tokens，最大輸出為 393,216 個 tokens，思考內容與最終答案共用此額度。模型 ID 為 qwen4-max-preview。

預覽期間，Qwen4-Max-Preview 僅限透過 Token Plan 使用

文件指出，Qwen4-Max-Preview 目前僅能透過 Token Plan 使用。開發者可選擇 Token Plan Personal 或 Token Plan Team，依照相應指南取得專用 API 金鑰，並使用專用 Base URL https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com。接著將模型 ID 設為 qwen4-max-preview。文件指出，各種協定的完整端點列於 Token Plan 指南中，該指南也涵蓋支援的用戶端、設定步驟及 Credits 優惠。

文件指出，預覽期間不會進行任何變更，且模型將在預覽結束後下架。

OpenAI Chat Completions 的輸出 Token 額度變更

從 qwen4-max-preview 開始，在 OpenAI Chat Completions API 中，max_tokens 等同於 max_completion_tokens。這兩個參數都會限制思考內容與最終答案所使用的 tokens 總數。由於思考內容會占用相同額度，先前僅依答案長度設定的上限可能會導致輸出遭截斷。現有 Qwen 模型維持原有行為。

在多輪對話中，Chat Completions 預設會啟用 preserve_thinking。歷史思考內容必須放在 assistant 訊息的 reasoning_content 欄位中回傳，不得串接到 content。視覺輸入、工具定義及結構化輸出格式的相關內容，請參閱 Model Studio 的其他文件頁面。

Qwen4-Max-Preview 主要規格與使用資訊

上下文長度：100 萬個 tokens

最大輸出：393,216 個 tokens，由思考內容與最終答案共用

思考功能：預設啟用；推理強度選項為 low、medium 或 xhigh（預設）

結構化輸出：JSON Object 和 JSON Schema

下架：模型將在預覽結束後下架

常見問題

開發者可以使用隨用隨付方式計費來使用 Qwen4-Max-Preview 嗎？

不行。文件指出，Qwen4-Max-Preview 目前處於預覽階段，僅能透過 Token Plan 使用，不支援隨用隨付。

Qwen4-Max-Preview 接受哪些輸入類型？

此模型接受文字、圖像及影片。文件列出的支援視覺與影片用途包括螢幕截圖分析、文件理解及影片分析。

使用 Chat Completions 搭配 Qwen4-Max-Preview 時，輸出上限如何計算？

在 OpenAI Chat Completions 中，此模型的 max_tokens 等同於 max_completion_tokens。兩者都會限制思考內容與最終答案的 tokens 總數，因此開發者設定上限時應預留思考內容所需的額度。

Qwen4-Max-Preview 的預覽期何時結束？

預覽期將持續至 2026 年 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8）。文件指出，模型將在預覽結束後下架。

GLM.content:
# Use Z.ai with the AI Gateway

Z.ai, formerly Zhipu AI, builds the open-weight GLM family of models for agents, reasoning, and coding.

Z.ai supports Chat Completions requests.

Z.ai is a built-in provider you can pay for with credits, so a provider key is optional. Add your own Z.ai key to bill usage to your Z.ai account instead of your ngrok.ai credits.

## Setup

### Create an access key and add credits
Follow the [quickstart](/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key and purchase [credits](/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### Store your Z.ai API key (optional)
Skip this step to pay with credits.
To bring your own key, create an API key in your [Z.ai](https://z.ai/model-api) account. Then [add a provider key](/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) and [create an access key configuration](/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with a `z-ai` routing rule that uses it.

### Send requests
Send requests with your access key:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="z-ai:glm-5.3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

QwenCloud, Tencent TokenHub, and Mistral AI also serve GLM models, so the `z-ai:` prefix keeps the request on Z.ai.

## Available models

See the model catalog.

GLM.content:
# Z.AI Coding Plan (Zhipu AI)

The Z.AI Coding Plan is a monthly subscription from Zhipu AI that gives you access to GLM models through an OpenAI-compatible API. GLM models are strong at text generation, deep thinking, and code — and the coding plan provides flat-rate access for use with AI coding tools.

## Why Z.AI?

- GLM model family — Access to GLM-5, GLM-4.7, and other variants
- OpenAI-compatible — Works with any tool that supports the OpenAI Chat Completions API
- International endpoint — Global access viaapi.z.ai
- Coding-optimized — Subscription designed for coding tool integration

## Available Models

Model | Capabilities 
---|---
glm-5 | Text generation, deep thinking 
glm-4.7 | Text generation, deep thinking 
glm-4.7-flash | Fast text generation 
glm-4.7-flashx | Fast text generation 
glm-4.6 | Text generation 
glm-4.6v | Text generation, visual understanding 
glm-4.5 | Text generation 
glm-4.5-air | Lightweight text generation 
glm-4.5-flash | Fast text generation 
glm-4.5v | Text generation, visual understanding 

::: tip Model Selection For general use, start withglm-5 — it's the most capable model. For faster responses, try glm-4.7-flash. Models ending in v support visual understanding (image input).
:::

## Quick Setup

### Step 1: Get Your API Key

- Go to Z.AI and sign in
- Navigate to your API key management page
- Create a new API key
- Copy the key (format:hexstring.Base64string)

### Step 2: Configure in Crow's Nest

- Open your Crow's Nest → Settings
- Find the AI Provider section
- Set:
- Provider: OpenAI (Z.AI uses an OpenAI-compatible API)
- API Key: Your Z.AI key
- Model:glm-5 (or any model from the table above)
- Base URL:https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4

- Click Save, then Test Connection
- Go to Messages → the AI Chat tab is now active

### Alternative:.env Configuration
AI_PROVIDER=openai
AI_API_KEY=your-zai-key-here
AI_MODEL=glm-5
AI_BASE_URL=https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4

No gateway restart needed — the config is hot-reloaded.

## Switching Models

To switch models, updateAI_MODEL in Settings or .env to any model from the table above. All models use the same API key and base URL — only the model name changes.

## Endpoint Reference

Purpose | URL 
---|---
Coding Plan (international) | https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4 
Standard API (international) | https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4 
Standard API (China mainland) | https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4 

::: warning The Coding Plan endpoint (/api/coding/paas/v4) is different from the standard API endpoint (/api/paas/v4). Use the correct one for your subscription type.
:::

## Troubleshooting

### "API key is invalid (401)"

Make sure you're using a Coding Plan key with the Coding Plan endpoint. Standard API keys don't work with the Coding Plan endpoint and vice versa.

### "Model not found (404)"

Check the model name matches exactly (case-sensitive). The available models depend on your subscription tier.

### Tool calls not working

GLM models generally support function/tool calling. If tools aren't working, tryglm-5 which has the strongest tool calling support.

GLM.content:
# Weekly AI Model Research Report — 2026-04-20

Scope of research window: ~2026-02-13 through 2026-04-20 (since last inventory refresh on 2026-04-18).

Current MJ inventory snapshot:

- metadata/ai-models/.ai-models.json: 109 models
- metadata/ai-models/.cohere-reranker-models.json: 2 reranker models
- metadata/ai-vendors/.ai-vendors.json: 23 vendors

The inventory was last refreshed on 2026-04-18 and is very current. Flagship pricing (GPT 5.4 at $2.50/$15, Grok 4.20 at $2/$6, Claude Opus 4.7 at $5/$25) all matches present market rates, so this cycle focused on incremental additions over the past ~10 weeks and newly-released open-weights models.

## Summary of Recommended Changes

Category | Count | Action 
---|---|---
New models to add | 5 | JSON edits 
Pricing changes | 0 | None verified 
Updated models (metadata) | 0 | None verified 
Deprecations (recommended) | 4 | Report-only, awaiting human review 
New vendors | 0 | All relevant vendors already present 
Flagged for human review | 7 | Report-only, no JSON changes 

## 1. New Models (JSON edits this PR)

### 1.1 GLM 5.1 (Z.AI / Zhipu AI)

- Release: 2026-04-07 (announcement), API GA on Z.AI and OpenRouter.
- Architecture: 744B total / 40B active MoE, 203K input context, 66K output tokens.
- License: MIT (open weights).
- Pricing (Z.AI direct): $0.95 / $3.15 per 1M tokens (input/output); cached input ~$0.19/1M.
- Positioning: Incremental refresh of GLM 5 (2026-02-11). Notable gains on SWE-bench Verified and AIME 2026 II vs GLM 5; same “Deep Thinking” mode.
- Action: Add new model row withPriorVersionID = GLM 5. Both Model Developer and Inference Provider vendor rows use VendorID = Z.AI.
- PowerRank: 21 (slightly above GLM 5 which is 20).

### 1.2 Gemma 4 31B Instruct (Google)

- Release: 2026-04-02.
- Architecture: Dense 31B, 256K context, multilingual (140+ languages), vision-in/text-out.
- License: Gemma Terms of Use (open weights).
- Pricing (Vertex AI / third-party hosts average): $0.13 / $0.38 per 1M tokens. (Most hosts price this identically; we attribute to Google as Model Developer and Vertex AI as Inference Provider.)
- Action: Add new model.PriorVersionID omitted — Gemma 3 lineage is not in inventory. PowerRank 8, SpeedRank 7, CostRank 4.

### 1.3 Gemma 4 26B A4B Instruct (Google)

- Release: 2026-04-02.
- Architecture: 26B total / 4B active MoE (A4B). Optimized for fast inference at lower cost. 256K context.
- License: Gemma Terms of Use (open weights).
- Pricing (Vertex AI): $0.08 / $0.35 per 1M tokens.
- Action: Add new model. PowerRank 7, SpeedRank 8, CostRank 3.

### 1.4 Cohere Rerank 4 Pro

- Release: 2025-12-16 (GA on Cohere API; missed in earlier cycles).
- Context: 32K tokens per document, 100+ languages.
- Pricing: $2.50 per 1K search units (Cohere standard rerank pricing).
- Action: Add to.cohere-reranker-models.json. Drives CohereReranker class, API name rerank-v4-pro. PowerRank 110 (above v3.5).
- Note: NoMJ: AI Model Costs record is being added. The existing rerankers (rerank-v3.5, rerank-multilingual-v3.0) also have no cost records, and the current AIModelPriceUnitType seed only contains Per 1M Tokens, Per 1K Tokens, Per 100K Tokens, Per Image — none of which fit per-search-unit rerank pricing. Pricing is documented in the model's Description field instead. A future migration could introduce a Per 1K Searches unit type.

### 1.5 Cohere Rerank 4 Fast

- Release: 2025-12-16.
- Context: 16K tokens per document, 100+ languages; distilled/faster variant of Rerank 4.
- Pricing: $1.50 per 1K search units.
- Action: Add to.cohere-reranker-models.json. API name rerank-v4-fast. PowerRank 90.
- Note: Same cost-record caveat as Rerank 4 Pro above.

## 2. Pricing Changes

None verified this cycle. All pricing checked against provider docs or reputable trackers on 2026-04-19 matches what is already in MJ. Notable checks:

- Anthropic: Opus 4.7 $5/$25; Sonnet 4.6 $3/$15 — unchanged.
- OpenAI: GPT 5.4 $2.50/$15; GPT 5.4-mini $0.40/$2; GPT 5.4-nano $0.10/$0.40 — unchanged.
- xAI: Grok 4.20 $2/$6 — unchanged.
- Google: Gemini 3.1 Pro, 3.1 Flash, 3.1 Flash-Lite — unchanged.
- MiniMax: M2.7 $0.30/$1.20 on Fireworks — unchanged.

## 3. Updated Models (Metadata Changes)

None recommended this cycle. No architecture, context window, or capability changes identified for existing models that weren't already captured.

## 4. Deprecated / Retired Models (Report-only, no JSON change)

Per provider documentation reviewed this week, the following models on Anthropic have entered retirement windows. NoIsActive=false flips in this PR — flagged for human review because MJ inventory may still want them available for historical/pinning use.

Model | MJ ID Reference | Provider Status | Recommendation 
---|---|---|---
Claude Sonnet 3.7 | present | Retirement scheduled by Anthropic for Q3 2026 | Leave active; consider flipping when Anthropic removes from API 
Claude Opus 3 | present | Retired on api.anthropic.com effective 2026-03 | Consider IsActive=false after human review 
Claude Sonnet 4 | present | Superseded by Sonnet 4.6; still served | Leave active 
Claude Opus 4 | present | Superseded by Opus 4.6 / 4.7; still served | Leave active 

Also noted but already historical:

- Gemini 1.5 Pro: Google's successor models (3.x) fully dominant, 1.5 still served via Vertex. No change recommended.

## 5. New Vendors

None this cycle. All vendors that surfaced in research are already present in.ai-vendors.json (confirmed: Z.AI, Google, Cohere, Black Forest Labs, MiniMax, Fireworks.ai, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Alibaba Cloud, Moonshot AI).

## 6. Flagged for Human Review (No JSON changes)

Items encountered during research that are ambiguous, gated, or otherwise not ready to be ingested as structured metadata:

- "Claude Mythos" — Appeared in third-party leak blogs in early April as Anthropic's rumored next-gen model. No official Anthropic page, no API availability. Do not add.
- DeepSeek V4 — Announcement-only from DeepSeek on 2026-03-28; API availability window was unstable/inconsistent during research. Context length and final pricing differed between the announcement and community trackers. Wait for stable GA + pricing confirmation.
- Meta "Muse Spark" — Announced by Meta on 2026-04-05 as a consumer product; no developer API, not a candidate for MJ. Do not add.
- Kimi K2.6 Preview (Moonshot AI) — Listed as preview/beta on platform.moonshot.ai; pricing was placeholder only ("preview — free during beta"). Wait for GA pricing.
- Qwen 3.6 Plus (Alibaba) — Listed on DashScope as "free preview"; no committed commercial pricing yet. Wait for GA pricing. (Note:Qwen 3.6 35B A3B is already in inventory from the 2026-04-18 update.)

GLM.content:
# GenAI Works的动态

Revolut wants to save costs and Claude is its first target. 💸 Its 2,000 engineers now code on GLM, an open model from Chinese lab Z.ai that Revolut runs on its own GPUs. The AI coding bill fell about 90% in under a year. Revolut's ops and infrastructure lead, David Abitbol, shared how at the AI Engineer conference in New York: → Flat billing, so no surprise invoices at the end of the month → Shorter context: 256K tokens is what engineers really need, even when a model can take 1 million → Speed: if a reply takes over 5 seconds, his Slack inbox blows up The biggest gains weren't in writing code. They came from debugging and clearing Jira and Confluence tickets. Frontier models didn't disappear either. A router still sends image tasks to Gemini or GPT. "The frontier is the exception," he said. Would your company trade the best model for a flat bill? 👇 Btw, Revolut's whole approach comes down to one question: does this task really need the most expensive model? If you can't answer that, you're probably overpaying for AI and still getting average results. GenAI Academy has hands-on courses that teach you to get real work out of AI, from prompting to building AI agents. Tell it your goal and it matches you with the right course in about a minute. Find your course: https://lnkd.in/eEssygGD

Model routing and predictable GPU economics beat chasing frontier benchmarks for routine engineering. Removing developer token caps unlocks real productivity across daily backlog and triage workflows.

Asking whether a task really needs the most expensive model is the AI version of not hiring a helicopter to cross the street. And a reply that takes over 5 seconds turning the Slack inbox into a bonfire is a performance review nobody asked for. That mindset fits https://www.chat-data.com/ well. Its model lineup runs from 0.5 credits per message (GPT 6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5) up to 17.5 for GPT 6 Astra, so you can match the model to the job. Every listed model has a 1M token window, which covers a 256K need with room to spare. Workflows also offer a max credits per visitor turn cap, and the Slack bot integration puts answers where teams already work.

"The frontier is the exception" matches how I actually work. I use Claude Code for the hard parts, like architecture, gnarly debugging and anything touching money or smart contracts, and lighter agents for the repetitive work around it. The skill isn't picking the best model, it's knowing which task deserves it. Same split in the real estate tools I build: drafting a listing description doesn't need a frontier model, but checking a contract clause or a price claim before it reaches a buyer does. Curious how Revolut's router decides when a coding task gets escalated, by task type or by failure?

Can you explain what happens to Slack inbox (“blows up”) if the reply takes more than 5 minutes? Thanks.

Daggubati Ashok Babu

Ecom system architect | Investor | Enthusiast in AI, Crypto, and Space | Independent Professional
现在 
Big models are worth it for only 2–3% of enterprise workloads(max 5 to 10%). Small, fine-tuned models can handle the other 90+%, faster and far cheaper. This shift is only getting started.

Most of the experienced developers would only need ai to "type" the code, not decide. Hence it's a good trade off.

Absolutely - mix of - stronger governance, hosted fixed cost models, cost tracking, best model fitment, caching, rate limits - are essential to how organizations need to adapt to the Tokenomics. https://lnkd.in/p/dGZXQJ6f

A 90% cost reduction is impressive, but maintaining code quality and developer productivity is what makes the switch sustainable.

I think Nik knows what he's doing.

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot Kimi

Source: https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/models/moonshot-kimi

Use Moonshot Kimi models for reasoning, chat, and coding through Runpod Public Endpoints, with supported inputs, outputs, and request examples.

Moonshot's Kimi family of models handles advanced reasoning and chat. It supports extended thinking with a visible reasoning trace before the final answer. A single endpoint serves five variants, each selected by setting themodel field in the request body.

[card] Try in playground

Test Moonshot Kimi in the Runpod Hub playground.

Endpoint | https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync 
---|---
Pricing | $4.00-$20.00 per 1M output tokens, $0.95-$4.00 per 1M input tokens 
Type | Text generation 

[!NOTE]

This endpoint is fully compatible with the OpenAI API. See the OpenAI compatibility examples below.

## Model variants

Choose a variant by setting themodel field in the request body (default kimi-k2.6). The endpoint slug stays moonshot-kimi for every variant.

model value | Description | Context window | Input price | Output price 
---|---|---|---|---
kimi-k2.6 (default) | General-purpose model with thinking and non-thinking modes, agentic capabilities, and multimodal input. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k2.7-code | Coding-focused model with thinking mode and agentic capabilities. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3 | Flagship model with always-on reasoning and configurable reasoning effort for long-horizon coding and knowledge work. | 1M (1,048,576 tokens) | $3.00 per 1M tokens | $15.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3.1-pro | Moonshot's 3T-class open-weight model with always-on reasoning, for long-horizon coding and agentic work. | 1M | $2.00 per 1M tokens | $10.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed | Kimi K3.1 Pro served for higher throughput, for interactive coding and agent loops. | 1M | $4.00 per 1M tokens | $20.00 per 1M tokens 

To target a variant other than the default, set themodel field to its ID. For example, to use the flagship model, set "model": "kimi-k3" in the request body (or model="kimi-k3" with the OpenAI SDK).

## Request

All parameters are passed within theinput object in the request body.

input.messagesarray required

Array of message objects with role and content.

input.messages[].rolestring required

The role of the message author. Usesystem, user, or assistant.

input.messages[].contentstring required

The content of the message.

input.modelstring (default: kimi-k2.6)

The Kimi variant to use. One ofkimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k3, kimi-k3.1-pro, or kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed.

input.sampling_params.max_tokensinteger (default: 2048)

Maximum number of tokens to generate. Kimi K3.1 models reason before they answer, and reasoning tokens count toward this limit. For coding tasks withkimi-k3.1-pro or kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed, set it to 8,192 or higher so the model has room to finish its answer.

input.sampling_params.temperaturefloat (default: 1)

Controls randomness in generation. Lower values make output more deterministic.

input.sampling_params.seedinteger

Seed for reproducible results.

input.sampling_params.top_kinteger

Restricts sampling to the top K most probable tokens.

input.sampling_params.top_pfloat

Nucleus sampling threshold. Range: 0.0-1.0.
